name: Calibrate Before Use
executive_summary: Correct for a model's baseline bias toward certain answers (caused by prompt format, example choice, and example order) before trusting its predictions, recovering large accuracy swings.
description: Estimates the model's output distribution on a content-free or trivial input (e.g. an empty test input) to measure its baseline bias toward particular labels, then uses that estimate to calibrate (reweight) the model's actual predictions. Demonstrates that few-shot accuracy on an identical task can swing from near-chance to near-state-of-the-art purely from prompt format, example selection, and example order — calibration recovers much of that variance without changing the prompt itself.
when_to_use: Few-shot classification-style tasks where label bias from prompt format/ordering is a plausible confound.
when_not_to_use: Open-ended generation tasks with no fixed label set to calibrate over.
known_pitfalls: Calibration corrects for measured bias on a specific baseline query; it does not fix an underlying reasoning error the model would make even under a corrected label prior.

primary_source.title: Calibrate Before Use: Improving Few-Shot Performance of Language Models
